title: Air-dry clay sea glass impression dish
subtitle: A small pinch pot with frosted sea-glass pieces pressed into the inner surface
excerpt: Sea glass pieces pressed into soft air-dry clay leave frosted translucent insets when the clay dries around them. The sea glass stays in place, held by the shrunken clay. The finished dish is a small trinket or jewellery tray, about 10 cm across.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Sea glass impression in clay.

glossaryTerms.definition: The stage when clay has firmed enough to hold its shape but is still slightly damp , the clay grips the sea glass pieces as it dries
Fully air-dried and ready for sealing

content.text: Sea glass pressed into soft clay sinks slightly below the surface. As the clay dries and shrinks, it grips the glass pieces from the sides. The result is a small dish with glass insets set flush in the clay. Use collected beach sea glass or buy craft sea glass from a hobby supplier. No kiln needed.
Forming the dish
Pinch 150 g of air-dry clay into a shallow bowl 10 cm across, about 2 cm deep. Keep walls at 7-8 mm thickness and the base flat by pressing it down on your work surface.
Smooth the inner surface with a damp sponge while the clay is still soft.
Pressing in the sea glass

Arrange the sea glass pieces on the inner surface of the bowl while the clay is still soft. Press each piece down firmly until it sits at least halfway into the clay. The flat face of each piece should be flush with or just below the clay surface.
Do not overlap pieces. Leave 1 cm of clay between each piece so the clay wall around each glass has enough thickness to hold it.
Press the clay gently against the sides of each glass piece with a wooden rib to ensure full contact. Do not press so hard that the dish distorts.
Drying
Set the dish on a flat board. Allow to air-dry without moving for the first 24 hours. Once
leather-hard
, check that the glass pieces are still seated firmly. As the clay shrinks it grips the glass. By
bone-dry
stage all pieces should be held without adhesive. If a piece is loose at bone-dry, remove it, add a small amount of PVA adhesive to the cavity, and replace.
Sealing

Seal the clay surfaces with two coats of diluted PVA. Avoid coating the glass unless you want a unified matte surface finish. Apply a clear gloss varnish over the glass pieces only for a polished look.
Variations
Use smooth pebbles or buttons instead of sea glass for different textures.
Press the glass into the outer wall of a coil-built pot rather than the inner base for a different placement.
Tint the clay body with a small amount of dark acrylic paint mixed in before pinching to make the glass stand out more against a darker background.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Glass pieces fell out at bone-dry stage
items.cause: Pieces not pressed deeply enough, or the clay was too dry when they were pressed in
items.fix: Work while the clay is freshly mixed and soft. Re-seat loose pieces with PVA adhesive once bone-dry

items.problem: Clay cracked around a large glass piece
items.cause: Large pieces do not allow enough clay shrinkage room and stress the clay
items.fix: Use sea glass pieces no larger than 3 cm. Press glass no deeper than halfway into the clay wall thickness
